literal: Than a minister who plots ruin, seventy crore enemies by one's side are better.
translation: Seventy crore open enemies by one's side are far better than a single minister who secretly plots one's ruin.
modern: கேடு விளைவிக்க நினைக்கும் அமைச்சரை விட, பக்கத்தில் இருக்கும் எழுபது கோடி பகைவர்கள் மேலானவர்கள்.
explanation: This couplet warns of the extreme danger posed by a treacherous minister. The word 'பழுது' means ruin or harm, and 'எண்ணும்' means plotting, describing a minister who secretly works against the ruler. The poet states that having seventy crore ('எழுபது கோடி') open enemies ('தெவ்') right next to oneself is actually preferable ('உறும்') to having one such traitor in the cabinet. An open enemy's hostility is visible and can be defended against, whereas an internal traitor destroys the state from within.
